info.title: Warehouse Designer API
info.description: Authoritative layout compiler and persistence for the 3D warehouse designer. The TypeScript compiler in packages/layout-core is the interactive mirror of the compiler used here; both are pinned by fixtures/layout-conformance.

schema.title: Response Health Db Health Db Get

post.description: Run the rules without writing anything. Used by the editor's diagnostics panel.
Compile and return the derived bins, checking the client hash if supplied.

schema.title: Response List Warehouses Api Warehouses Get

post.description:
Create a warehouse, optionally seeding it with a document.

When ``doc`` is supplied it wins outright — including its own footprint — because
the document is the source of truth and a payload whose footprint disagreed with
its document would otherwise create two conflicting records.

put.description: Autosave. Debounced by the client; guarded by the revision token here.

delete.description:
Throw the draft away, keeping any published version intact.

A discard bumps the revision too: a client that still holds the old token must
find out that its working copy is no longer the server's.

post.description: Compile without writing. The editor's pre-flight for a save or a publish.

schema.title: Response Validate Warehouse Layout Api Warehouses  Warehouse Id  Validate Post

post.description:
Validate, materialise and publish in one transaction.

Idempotent on ``doc_hash``: publishing the document that is already live returns
the existing version with ``changed: false``.

schema.title: Response List Versions Api Warehouses  Warehouse Id  Versions Get

get.description:
The published layout for Operate mode.

Bins are read from the materialised rows rather than recompiled, because those
rows carry the surrogate ids that placements reference. The document is also
recompiled and its hash returned alongside, so a snapshot that no longer matches
what the compiler would produce today is visible as ``conflicts`` instead of
being silently served.

schema.title: Response List Skus Api Warehouses  Warehouse Id  Skus Get

put.description:
Edit a SKU in place.

This does **not** re-validate existing placements. Shrinking a SKU cannot invalidate
anything, but growing one can, and silently deleting inventory because a dimension
changed would be worse than leaving a placement that a later check flags. The
placement list reports each bin's utilisation, so an over-capacity bin is visible.

schema.title: Response List Warehouse Placements Api Warehouses  Warehouse Id  Placements Get

post.description:
Place a SKU in a bin, revalidating on the server.

The client checks the same thing before the drop, so a 200 here means both sides
agreed and a 422 means the codes should match what the client computed.
Fill many bins at once, with a verdict per bin rather than all-or-nothing.

BinPlacementsOut.title: BinPlacementsOut
BinPlacementsOut.description:
A bin and everything in it, with the capacity arithmetic already done.

`remaining*` is computed from the *other* placements, so the client can render a
drag ghost from the same numbers the server checks rather than re-deriving them.

BulkPlacementOut.title: BulkPlacementOut
BulkPlacementOut.description: Every bin gets its own verdict: a bulk fill is per-bin, not all-or-nothing.

PublishedLayoutOut.title: PublishedLayoutOut
PublishedLayoutOut.description:
What Operate mode reads.

Bins come from the materialised rows rather than from a fresh compile, because
those rows carry the surrogate ids that placements reference. ``docHash`` and
``recompiledDocHash`` are both returned so drift between the snapshot and the
current compiler is visible instead of assumed away.

UtilizationOut.title: UtilizationOut
UtilizationOut.description: Heatmap input: utilisation per bin, and the bins that hold nothing.

WarehouseCreate.title: WarehouseCreate
WarehouseCreate.description:
A warehouse starts from a footprint, with an optional first document.

Supplying ``doc`` lets the client seed a new warehouse from the layout it already
has open instead of round-tripping a blank one through a draft save.
